record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Is every quasi Riemann surface Q isomorphic to the space D_int_0(Σ) of integral 0-currents on some ordinary two-dimensional conformal space Σ with the same Jacobian, and if so how can that isomorphism be constructed concretely?

evidence.quote: Conjecturally, every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic to D_int_0(Σ) for Σ the 2d conformal space with the same Jacobian as Q, the Jacobian being the complex torus made from the homology in the middle dimension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a quasi Riemann surface Q to be a metric abelian topological group equipped with the additional structure (intersection form, complex structure on its middle-dimensional homology, and graded spaces of integral j-currents for j = 0, 1, 2, 3 with their weak metrics) abstracting the properties of the spaces of integral 0-currents on a 2-dimensional conformal manifold. To any 2-dimensional conformal space Σ, associate the abelian topological group D_int^0(Σ) of integral 0-currents of finite total mass on Σ, equipped with its natural weak metric, and define the Jacobian J(Q) (respectively J(Σ)) to be the complex torus built from the middle-dimensional homology together with its complex structure.

Question: Is it true that every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic, as a quasi Riemann surface, to D_int^0(Σ) for some 2-dimensional conformal space Σ whose ordinary Jacobian J(Σ) is isomorphic to J(Q)? If so, give a concrete construction of Σ from Q and of the isomorphism Q ≅ D_int^0(Σ).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is stated in Daniel Friedan's papers on quasi Riemann surfaces (2017) as an open conjecture, and no proof or counterexample appears in the literature. It remains an unresolved conjecture used as motivation in subsequent discussions.

status_evidence.title: Quasi Riemann surfaces II. Questions, comments, speculations
status_evidence.snippet: Every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic to the quasi Riemann surface Q(Σ) associated to a unique two-dimensional conformal space Σ whose ordinary Jacobian J(Σ) is isomorphic to J(Q).
status_evidence.claim: The statement is formulated as a conjecture, not as a proven theorem.

status_evidence.title: Quasi Riemann surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Prototypes are the spaces of integral 0-currents on a Riemann surface; the classification conjecture would hold if any two quasi Riemann surfaces with isomorphic Jacobians are isomorphic.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of quasi Riemann surfaces by their Jacobians is posed as an open conjecture.
